title: Meet a new classmate
prompt: Write a short dialogue between two invented classmates. Greet each other, ask names, spell one name and say goodbye. Use an imaginary phone number if you include one.
checks: I used a greeting and an introduction.
I included a spelling question.
I used capital letters for names.
I ended with a goodbye.

title: A friendly email
prompt: Write an email about an invented person and their family. Include a country, ages, two family relationships and a birthday day. You can use fictional names.
checks: I used am, is and are correctly.
I included family words.
I used my, his, her or our clearly.
I capitalized countries and days.

title: My world
prompt: Describe an invented student’s possessions, pet and school. Include colours, one thing the student has not got, favourite subjects and a timetable day.
checks: I used have got or has got.
I included a negative with haven’t or hasn’t.
I put adjectives before nouns.
I included school subjects and a day.

title: A day and a hobby
prompt: Describe an invented student’s typical day. Give four times and two free-time activities. Ask two questions about the student’s routine and answer them.
checks: I used at with times and on with days.
I checked third-person -s.
I included don’t or doesn’t.
I used do or does in questions.

title: A room and a town
prompt: Describe an imaginary bedroom and a town. Give three furniture locations, name three places in the town and say what a visitor can and cannot do there.
checks: I used there is and there are.
I described locations with prepositions.
I used can or can’t plus a base verb.
My descriptions are clear without a book picture.

title: Usually and today
prompt: Write about two invented people. Describe their appearance and clothes, say what they usually do on Saturday and what they are doing now. Add a short conversation buying one item of clothing.
checks: I used be for height and have got for hair or eyes.
I used present simple for a habit.
I used am/is/are + -ing for now.
I used is or are correctly when asking a price.
